newsitem.title: USA: Philly stock exchange may raise public membership.
newsitem.headline: Philly stock exchange may raise public membership.

text.p: The Philadelphia Stock Exchange (PHLX) is likely to increase the public representation on its board by the time the next board is chosen in March 1997, the head of a special investigating committee at the exchange said.
"I think you will see the the percentages change by the next election," J. Carter Beese, a PHLX board member and vice chairman of Alex Brown International, said in a telephone interview.

Beese headed a PHLX committee investigating conflict-of- interest accusations against the exchange's chairman, Vincent Casella, who resigned on Wednesday after the PHLX board heard the committee's report.
The committee was formed to investigate Casella's financial ties to Ashton Technology Group Inc, a subsidiary of which was hired to build a trading system on the exchange's equity floor.
Casella was listed in documents submitted to federal regulators has holding 152,000 shares in Ashton shortly before it went public.

In announcing the resignation, the exchange said the committee also recommended increasing public representation on the exchange's board, which currently consists of 29 members, 26 of whom are traders at the exchange.

In addition, Beese said on Thursday, the committee recommended reviewing and updating PHLX bylaws and regulations "with an eye toward eliminating any ambiguities that may exist because of some anachronistic regulations."

He declined to discuss how any conflicts of interest may have escaped board detection, saying he could not reveal the substance of the investigation. But the findings of the probe would be shared with the federal Securities and Exchange Commission. Beese is a former member of the commission.
Beese said the PHLX, an internationally leading marketplace for foreign currency options, would emerge from the turmoil with an enhanced reputation.
"I think its reputation has been enhanced. It shows that we take our self-regulatory responsibilty very seriously," he said.
